modules.name: auth
modules.summary: Who is using the app. The Kernel owns accounts and sessions; the app only reads the current one.
notes: Visibility decides who may open the app shell. It never grants data access on its own.

An app account has no role the Kernel keeps. An app that needs an administrator keeps roles in its own table, keyed by the account ID that actor.id binds, and its owner names the first one with SQL in the editor's Data panel.

The Deployment's Signup Policy, which the owner sets in the editor or with signup_policy_set, decides who may create an account: Open, Invitation only, Closed or an Allowlist. Under Invitation only, the sign-in page offers no account creation; invited people accept from the link in their email, which opens /_konae/invitation. On an installation whose development transport sends no email, the owner's invitation call answers that link as acceptUrl, once, for the owner to hand over. A pending person who signs in with the right password, or with Google, is told that an invitation is waiting.

The owner may add Continue with Google to the sign-in page in the editor's Access > Users view or with sign_in_methods_set, once the app's own Google client ID and secret are set. A Google sign-in reaches the app account that holds the same email, with the same actor.id as the password, and the Signup Policy decides whether an email without an account gets one. Google proves only Gmail addresses and addresses of a Google Workspace domain; any other address signs in with email and password. Password sign-in stays on.

modules.name: actions
modules.summary: The only door to the database. A call names a Server Action declared in actions.json and passes its input; the Kernel authorizes the caller, binds the input and runs the action's one SQL statement, or records its Signal.
notes: A binding passes who calls: { "source": "actor", "field": "id" } is the signed-in person's ID or the API key's ID, and refuses a caller without one. It cannot come from the input. Roles are rows in the app's own tables, checked in SQL against that ID.
A query action returns the rows of its SELECT. Column names are exactly the ones the SELECT projects, so alias any expression the app reads.
A mutation action returns { changes, lastInsertId }. Read changed rows with a separate query. A mutation that declares a guard and changes no row is refused with the guard instead.

The Action Contract, action-contract.json, lists every action with its inputs, the columns it returns, its errors and limits. It is written from actions.json and schema.sql by konae contract and carried in the export; an expression the SELECT returns without AS has no name in it, and the Validation Gate warns.

To record that something happened, such as a signup to a newsletter or a finished lesson, declare a signal on the mutation that does it, or add an action of kind signal and call it with miniapp.actions.call. There is no other tracking call.
A call the Kernel refuses records no Signal and counts in no Usage total, except a guard's refusal, which Usage counts under refused.

To email someone when something happens, such as a booking or an alert, declare notify on the mutation that does it. It reaches the owner, the person who called the action, or the verified accounts a column of the changed rows names, nobody else.

declarations.summary: Each kind takes its own top-level keys. A query takes kind, access, statement, bindings and http. A mutation takes kind, access, statement, bindings, http, signal, guard, notify and schedule. A signal action takes kind, access, bindings, signal and an empty statement. A call takes kind, access, bindings, url, method, body, headers, auth, then and an empty statement. Any other key is refused, so a misspelled or misplaced key cannot pass and do nothing. A key set to null counts as absent. A key with its own refusal, such as a guard on a query, gets that refusal instead. The Validation Gate and the Kernel refuse the same declarations with the same messages.

When the action succeeds, and for a mutation only when it changed at least one row, the Kernel records the Signal with the named inputs as its properties, in the Deployment's Usage store. The property actor records the caller's ID: the user's, the API key's, or null for a visitor or a signed request. A signal action runs no SQL and returns { recorded: true }. The owner reads Signals with signals_read; the app cannot. The Validation Gate and the Kernel refuse the same declarations with the same messages.

declarations.summary: "guard": "<message>" on a mutation. When its statement changes no row, the Kernel refuses the call with that message instead of answering { changes: 0, lastInsertId: 0 }: a tool error for miniapp.actions.call, 403 on an HTTP route. Usage counts the call under refused, and no Signal is recorded. Write the app's rule into the statement's WHERE, such as "the caller is an organizer" or "the slot is free", and the guard is what the person sees when the rule says no. Without a guard, a mutation that changes no row answers { changes: 0, lastInsertId: 0 }. The Validation Gate and the Kernel refuse the same declarations with the same messages.

declarations.summary: "notify": { "to": "owner" or "actor" or { "column": "<name>" }, "changes": ["<column>", ...], "subject": "<template>", "body": "<template>" } on a mutation; "changes" is optional. When its statement changes a row, the Kernel queues email: to the app's contact email in konae.json, which the owner sets in App settings or with contact_email_set and a first publish from Konae fills with the owner's email when Konae knows it, to the calling account's email when that account proved it by answering a verification, invitation or recovery link, or, with to: { column }, one email to each such account of this app whose ID a changed row holds in that column, listing only that account's rows. It never sends to an address from the input or from a row: a column value is an account ID, and a value that is not a verified account of this Deployment sends nothing. The templates may use {input.<key>} for one of the action's input bindings, {actor.id}, {kernel.now} (the time of the call or run, as 2026-11-08 07:00 UTC), {changes.count} (rows changed, or the recipient's own rows with to: { column }) and, in the body only, {changes}: one line per changed row with the "changes" columns joined by " · ", at most 50 lines and then "- and <n> more". The Kernel reads the rows back by appending its own RETURNING to the statement, so the columns belong to the table the statement changes; the author still writes no RETURNING, and the answer stays changes and lastInsertId. A value loses its line breaks, keeps 200 characters and is escaped in the HTML part. The mutation answers as it would without notify, and an email that cannot be sent never fails it: Usage counts every notice under notify as "<action>: queued" or "<action>: <reason>", and the owner reads the queue with mail_status. Scheduled runs and a call's then mutation also process notify when they change rows. They have no caller, so to owner and to { column } work and to actor records no-account. The editor preview sends no email. The Validation Gate and the Kernel refuse the same declarations with the same messages.
limits: a subject template is 1 to 120 characters on one line; a body template is 1 to 2000 characters
a placeholder's value keeps 200 characters on one line; a rendered subject keeps 200 characters and a body 5,000
notices count apart from account email: 200 a day per app, 500 a day per owner and 50 a day per recipient from one app, and every email counts toward the installation's 1,000 a day
nothing is sent while the installation's sender preflight is not ready; the notice is recorded as failed with sender-not-ready

changes names 1 to 8 columns; {changes} lists at most 50 rows per notice
one run reads back at most 1,000 changed rows and writes to at most 50 accounts through to: { column }, in account ID order; each account past the 50th counts under notify as recipient-cap

declarations.summary: "schedule": { "every": "15m" } or { "every": "6h" } or { "daily": "02:00" } on a mutation that takes no input. The Kernel's own timer runs it once in each period, or once a day at that UTC time, with no caller: an actor binding is null, kernel.now is the time of the run, and literals bind as written. Use it for work that must happen when nobody asks, such as releasing a hold that lapsed or closing a day. A run that changes no row had nothing to do, so the guard does not apply; a run that changed a row records the action's Signal with actor null. A changed run also processes notify through the notice queue. Use to owner, or to { column } to reach the accounts the changed rows name; to actor records no-account because the timer has no caller. A run queues one notice per recipient, and {changes} lists the rows it changed, so a digest can say what is due. The owner reads each run, with its outcome and changes, under scheduled with usage_read. Only the timer runs it: a call through miniapp.actions.call or actions_invoke is refused with "Action <name> runs only on its schedule.", unless the action also declares an http route, which answers as its callers say. The Validation Gate and the Kernel refuse the same declarations with the same messages. The editor preview runs no schedule; konae dev and a Deployment do.
limits: every runs from 5 minutes to 24 hours; periods count from 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC, so a period that divides the day, such as every 15m, runs at :00, :15, :30 and :45
one run per period: a Kernel that was down for several periods runs the action once when it is back, and a restart does not run it again in the same period
publishing never runs it; the first run is at the next period
a run takes the app's data lock and has the 2-second statement budget
a run that fails is retried at the next tick, once a minute, and the Deployment's runs never overlap
an app in maintenance runs nothing, and runs once when it leaves it
the Kernel keeps the newest 10,000 runs per Deployment; usage_read returns the newest 500 in its range

modules.name: files
modules.summary: Small files stored by the Kernel for one Deployment. The manifest can require an app session to read every file.
notes: By default, only the uploader can list or read a private file.
On a public Deployment a signed-out visitor can list and read public files. On a private Deployment any signed-in user can.

files.list returns metadata and the same-origin file path without reading file bytes. files.upload sends the file's bytes in one request and returns its path as url. The Kernel checks access on every file request, including conditional requests.

The uploader alone changes a file's visibility with files.update or deletes it with files.delete. A deleted file stops counting against the Deployment's file quota and its ID answers File not found from then on, through every door.

The operator of the installation sets the per-file limit and the Deployment's file quota. The defaults are 2 MiB per file and 20 MiB per Deployment, and a refusal names the limits in force. Do not promise the defaults in an app's text.

A visitor without a session on a private Deployment is asked to sign in before any file is looked up: 401 authentication-required. On a public Deployment, a file the visitor may not read answers 404 File not found, the same as a missing one. A signed-in user who may not read a file also gets 404.

declarations.summary: Set "fileAccess": "app-users" to let every signed-in user of this app read its files, including earlier uploads. The same rule applies to file listings and direct file URLs. IDs stay valid. The uploader keeps deletion rights.

modules.name: calls
modules.summary: Calls from this app to another app or an outside service, made by the Kernel from its own process, never from the browser. There is no browser call: the page invokes the call action with miniapp.actions.call, which answers { callId, queued: true }, and the Kernel sends the request, retries it and runs the then mutation with the answer.
notes: The Kernel resolves an outside host once per attempt and refuses it when any address it resolves to is loopback, private, link-local (where cloud metadata answers), shared, documentation, benchmarking, multicast, reserved, unspecified, unique-local, or an IPv4 address carried in IPv6. It then connects to the address it checked, so a second DNS answer cannot redirect the request.
http is allowed only to an app of this installation, which the Kernel reaches in its own process. Every other URL must be https.
Each attempt of a signed call signs again with a new nonce, so a retry is never refused as a replay.
An app in maintenance sends no call and runs no then mutation until maintenance ends.
Usage counts each queued call under call, by action. The then mutation counts as an action, or under refused when its guard refuses, and records its Signal with actor null.
The editor preview answers { callId, queued: true } and sends nothing. Run calls on konae dev, or on a Deployment.

declarations.summary: { "kind": "call", "access", "bindings": [input bindings only], "method": "GET" | "POST", "url": "https://inbox-2.apps.example.org/hooks/events", "body"?: { "<body key>": "<input key>" | { "value": <constant> } }, "headers"?: { "Idempotency-Key": "<input key>" | { "value": <constant> } }, "auth"?: { "secret": "<name>", "header"?: "X-Inbox-Signature" } | { "key": "<name>" }, "then"?: { "action": "<mutation>", "inputs": { "<input key>": "<JSON pointer>" } } }. A POST sends the body keys as a JSON object and a GET as query parameters after the URL's own; a null or missing input leaves its key out, and a constant, a string of at most 1000 characters, a number, a boolean or null, is sent as actions.json writes it, so the caller cannot change it. On POST, a body key with dotted segments such as line_items.0.price expands into nested JSON, so a Checkout Session can name line items without a free-form object. headers may set only Idempotency-Key, from an input or a constant, for providers that require it. auth.secret signs the request with Konae's route scheme in the header, X-Konae-Signature unless header names another; auth.key sends the secret's value, an API key, as Authorization: Bearer. The secret's value stays in the Kernel; it never reaches the browser, the artifact or an export. When the call ends, delivered or failed, the then mutation runs once with no actor, its inputs read by JSON pointers from { ok, status, error, body, input }: ok is true for a 2xx answer, status the HTTP status or null, error the Kernel's error kind or null, body the answer parsed as JSON or null, and input the call's own inputs. A then mutation runs only after its call. A URL whose host is an app of this installation goes through that app's route code in the Kernel's process, with the same callers check, signature check, guard, Usage and Signal. The owner reads every call with calls_read. The Validation Gate and the Kernel refuse the same declarations with the same messages, except the three marked as the Kernel's alone.
limits: 20 calls queued per app in any 60 seconds, unless the installation sets KONAE_CALLS_PER_MINUTE
10 seconds per attempt, from connecting to the last byte of the answer
64 KiB per answer; a larger one ends the call as failed with answer-too-large
5 attempts for a network failure, a timeout, 408, 425, 429 or a 5xx, waiting 30 seconds, then 1, 2 and 4 minutes; any other answer is final
no redirect is followed: a 3xx is the answer
the outbox keeps the newest 1000 finished calls per app and the first 1 KiB of each answer

declarations.summary: "connects": ["https://api.example.com"] in the project manifest, or manifest.connects in konae.json. Each origin is added to the page's connect-src, so the page may fetch it directly: another app's public GET route, which answers with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, or an outside API that allows the app's origin. Nothing else is loosened. A key or a secret never goes to the browser: a request that needs one is a call action, which the Kernel sends.
limits: 10 origins

errors.message: connects must be a list of at most 10 origins, such as ["https://api.example.com"].
errors.when: connects is not a list of strings or lists more than 10

errors.message: connects lists <key>, which is not an origin. Write it as https://host or https://host:port, with no path; http only for a host under localhost.
errors.when: an entry is not exactly an origin: http to a host outside localhost, a path or trailing slash, a wildcard, capitals, or the default port written out

errors.message: connects lists <key> twice.
errors.when: an origin appears twice

modules.name: http
modules.summary: Routes on the Deployment's own host for programs and other services: a JSON endpoint, a webhook, a file a program fetches. There is no browser call; the app's own pages keep using miniapp.actions.call, and may use a file's route as an img src.
notes: Only an action declared anonymous may bind a route. A route has three kinds of caller: a service that signs the request (signature), a program that sends Authorization: Bearer with an API key the owner issued (key), and a person signed in to the app, from the app's own origin (session). An actor binding yields the key's ID or the user's ID; a signed request has no actor.

Without callers, a signed route takes the signature or a key, an unsigned route on a private app a key or a session, and an unsigned route on a public app anyone. A person whose session the route does not take must sign like any sender.
An action whose route does not answer anyone answers only on that route: miniapp.actions.call refuses it. The app's own page calls such a route with fetch, which sends the session cookie.

A signed route reads the declared header as t=<unix seconds>,n=<nonce>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256>. The MAC is keyed with the secret and covers t, the nonce, the method, the path, the canonical query string and the raw body, joined by newlines. The canonical query string is the pairs sorted by key, then value, written as application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

A provider's scheme. hmac-body: the header carries the prefix, if declared, then the HMAC of the raw body with the declared algorithm, in hex or base64 (GitHub: X-Hub-Signature-256, sha256, hex, prefix sha256=; Shopify: X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256, sha256, base64). timestamped: the header carries comma-separated fields, the timestamp after prefix and the hex HMAC-SHA256 of <t>.<body> after tag (Stripe: Stripe-Signature, t=, v1=, window 300). svix: svix-id, svix-timestamp and svix-signature, the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of <id>.<t>.<body> keyed with the base64 after whsec_ (Resend, Svix). A provider's delivery is accepted once; one whose action fails is forgotten, so the provider's retry runs. A long form with several wrong keys is refused once, with one sentence per key in the order the parse checks them: keys the scheme does not take, the header, the secret, then the scheme's settings.

A provider's preset. { "provider": "github" | "shopify" | "stripe" | "svix", "secret": "<name>" } stands for that provider's long form: github for hmac-body over X-Hub-Signature-256 with sha256, hex and prefix sha256=; shopify for hmac-body over X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 with sha256 and base64; stripe for timestamped over Stripe-Signature with t=, v1= and window 300; svix for svix, which Resend also uses. A preset takes no other key, so a route has one spelling. Both doors read the table from kernel-rs/kernel/src/signature-presets.json, and each row verifies a published or provider-form vector. Any other sender uses the long form.

fields maps an input key to a JSON path into the POST body, such as { "id": "$.data.object.id" }. Each input fields does not name is read from the body's key of that name, and every other key of the body is left out, so a provider's payload needs no adapter. A path that is missing leaves its input out: a required one is refused as missing, a nullable one binds NULL.
The owner sets the secret with the secret_set owner tool before publishing. It never appears in actions.json, the Build Artifact or an export.

GET /_konae/files/<id>, the path miniapp.files.url returns under the page's base path, answers a file the caller may read, with its own type. A person reads by the usual file rules, a visitor reads public files of a public app, and an API key reads the visibilities the owner named on it. A visitor without a session on a private app gets 401 authentication-required before any file is looked up; every other caller who may not read the file gets 404 File not found, the same as for a missing or deleted one.
The editor preview serves no routes. Run them on konae dev, or on a Deployment.

declarations.summary: { "method": "GET" | "POST", "path": "/api/items", "signature"?: { "scheme"?: "konae" | "hmac-body" | "timestamped" | "svix", "header": "X-Signature", "secret": "items_webhook", ... }, "callers"?: ["signature" | "key" | "session"], "fields"?: { "<input key>": "$.data.object.id" } } on an action declared anonymous. GET binds a query and maps the query string onto its input bindings by type; POST binds a mutation and reads a JSON object body. A signature's scheme is konae by default; hmac-body, timestamped and svix verify a provider's own webhook, such as GitHub's, Shopify's, Stripe's or Resend's. fields reads each named input from a JSON path into the body, and with it the route leaves out body keys no input names. callers names who may call the route; without it a signed route takes the signature or an API key, an unsigned route on a private Deployment an API key or a session, and an unsigned route on a public Deployment anyone. An action whose route does not answer anyone answers only on that route, never through miniapp.actions.call. The route answers { result } with the rows or { changes, lastInsertId }, and { error } with a status code. The Validation Gate and the Kernel refuse the same declarations with the same messages.
limits: a POST body of 64 KiB
a signature's t within 300 seconds of the Kernel's clock, a nonce of 1 to 64 letters, digits, - and _, and each signature accepted once

a provider's scheme: an hmac-body MAC accepted once in 72 hours, a timestamped t within its window of 1 to 3600 seconds, a svix timestamp within 300 seconds and its id accepted once in 72 hours, and at most 4 signature values in a header
fields: 1 to 32 inputs, each path $ and 1 to 16 .name or [index] steps, up to 200 characters
the runtime endpoint's action rate limits: 30 per 10 seconds per client address without a key or session, 120 per 10 seconds per user or key
50 live API keys per Deployment

errors.message: Action <name> is a signal action, so it takes no route. To record a signal from an HTTP route, declare the signal on a mutation with a POST route.
errors.when: a signal action declares http

errors.message: Action <name> must bind GET for a query and POST for a mutation.

errors.message: Action <name> is authenticated, so it cannot declare http. Only anonymous actions answer on an HTTP route.
errors.when: the action's access is authenticated

errors.when: the path is "/", ends with "/", climbs with "..", or carries a query string

errors.message: Actions <name> and <name> both bind <key>.

errors.when: the secret is not a secret name

errors.message: Action <name> has an invalid http binding.
errors.when: http is not an object, has another key, or its signature has a key other than header and secret

errors.when: the signature's scheme is another word, or not text

errors.message: Action <name> has an invalid <key> signature. It takes <names>.

errors.message: Action <name> binds GET, so its signature must use the konae scheme. A provider's scheme signs a POST body.
errors.when: a query's route declares hmac-body, timestamped or svix

errors.message: Action <name> names an unknown signature provider. Use <names>.
errors.when: the signature's provider is not text or not a row of the preset table, in that letter case; <names> is the table's rows, "github", "shopify", "stripe" or "svix"

errors.message: Action <name> names the signature provider "<key>", so its signature takes only "provider" and "secret". Remove <names>.
errors.when: a preset has a long-form key beside it, such as header or scheme; the refusal names every such key in sorted order

errors.message: Action <name> has an invalid signature algorithm. Use "sha256" or "sha1".
errors.when: an hmac-body signature names no algorithm or another one

errors.message: Action <name> has an invalid signature encoding. Use "hex" or "base64".
errors.when: an hmac-body signature names no encoding or another one

errors.message: Action <name> has an invalid signature prefix. Use 1 to 32 letters, digits, "=", "-", "_", "." or ":", such as "sha256=".
errors.when: an hmac-body signature's prefix has another character or is longer

errors.message: Action <name> has an invalid timestamp prefix. Use the field's name and "=", such as "t=".
errors.when: a timestamped signature has no prefix, or one that is not a name and =

errors.message: Action <name> has an invalid signature tag. Use the field's name and "=", such as "v1=", other than the timestamp's.
errors.when: a timestamped signature has no tag, one that is not a name and =, or the timestamp's

errors.message: Action <name> has an invalid signature window. Use a whole number of seconds from 1 to 3600.
errors.when: a timestamped signature has no window, or one that is not a whole number from 1 to 3600

errors.message: Action <name> binds GET, so it cannot declare fields. Fields read a POST body.
errors.when: a query's route declares fields

errors.message: Action <name> has an invalid fields map. Map 1 to 32 input keys to JSON paths, such as "$.data.object.id".
errors.when: fields is not an object, is empty or has more than 32 keys

errors.message: Action <name> maps <key>, which is not one of its input bindings.

errors.message: invalid-signature

errors.message: This route does not accept API keys.

errors.message: replayed-signature
errors.when: the same signature arrives a second time, or a svix id again within 72 hours; a retry signs again with a new nonce, and a provider's delivery whose action failed is not remembered (409)

errors.message: invalid-api-key
